title: Part Two, Chapter 11: The Head of Hun-ahpu

verses.t: And then, calling all the animals, the coati, the peccary, all of them, small and great, in the night and toward morning, he said to them, "I have called you to assign each of you your food." This is what Xbalanque said to them. "Take your food." And they said, "Very well," and then each went to take possession of its food, as they all came to show themselves. Some took rotten things for food, others grasses, others stones, others earth; different were the foods of the animals, great and small. And last of all came one that was a turtle, which came waddling along to take its food; and this was put in place of Hun-ahpu's head, and then its eyes were carved. And a great many sages came from the sky; the Heart of the Sky came, and Huracán came; to the house of bats they came. And so its face was finished; it turned out very good and very handsome, and it spoke as well. And when it was about to dawn, when the sky was growing light, it was said to the vulture, "Darken it again." And the old one said, "Very well," and then it grew dark; four times the old vulture darkened it. And so they say now that the vulture streaks the sky when it is about to dawn. And so it was cool when it began to be made. "Yes, it will be good," they said, when Hun-ahpu was made. And he said, "It will be good," and so his head would be bone as before, and it was made as if it were his head. And afterwards they agreed together that they would not really play ball: "You only make a show of playing; I alone shall do it," said Xbalanque to him. And then he gave orders to a rabbit and said to it, "Go, stay there in the ball court, and get into the tomato patch," it was said to the rabbit by Xbalanque. "And when the rubber ball comes to you, come out at once, for I shall do what I have to do." This was said to the rabbit when it was given its orders that night. And when it dawned, both of them were well.

And when the ball was thrown, the head of Hun-ahpu was in the ball court. "Now you are beaten; now it is done; now you have given in," it was said to him; and Hun-ahpu only crouched. And it was a new head of rubber, as it is called, and it felt no pain; they only made a show. And as soon as the lords of the underworld threw the rubber ball, Xbalanque went out to meet it, and the ball went straight to the yoke and stopped there, and went out very fast; it passed over the ball court and went straight to the tomato patch. And then the rabbit came out leaping, and then all those of the underworld went after it with a great noise and shouting; they went after the rabbit. And then Hun-ahpu's head was taken, and Xbalanque put it back in place, and went and set the turtle over the ball court. And it was his head, the head of Hun-ahpu, and at this both of them were glad. And then those of the underworld went to look for the rubber ball, which had already been caught there in the tomato patch. And then they were called: "Come, here is our rubber ball; we have found it," they said in their fashion. And as those of the underworld came, they said, "What is this? What have we seen?" And then they began to play ball; both of them were playing ball. And then the turtle was struck by Xbalanque, and it went smashing to pieces in the ball court, and was broken into seeds before them. And those of the underworld said, "Who will go after it and bring it back?" And such was the defeat, the vanquishing of the lords of the underworld by Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque; and though they were in great trouble, they did not die, with all that was done to them.
